_readme: Numa's pattern library: 31 hook patterns (docs/research/R1_Hooks.md), 16 script structures (R3), 12 carousel templates and 9 single-photo types (R4), plus CTA, offer-framing and growth seeds (spec and the developer-kit research). Seeded by strategy.py's research importer and corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md, where Numa's facts and rules win: 'Numa' never 'NUMA', plunges 44-52°F and sauna 175-190°F, no stated sauna capacity, no Clinical Conversations (cancelled), no emojis, no trending songs (trend-audio-sync became beat-sync-original-sound), member words photo-led only (no quote cards), no unconfirmed amenities (robes, tea, lockers), R4's yoga-studio copy replaced (its slide structure kept). owner_signal records what the owners' own posts showed (real people, collabs, walk-out lines, event recaps and member testimony worked; graphics and posters flopped): those priors count more than research. Hook priority follows R1's 'The 10 to Test First' (those and the owners' winners start as testing, the rest as candidates, so 3-5 arms are tested at a time, R6). No seed is 'proven': that is earned only from Numa's own posts (strategy.py learn). Every example and template passes claims_scan.py (tests/unit/test_strategy.py). This file changes only with a plugin release; learned statuses live in STATE/strategy.json.

patterns.name: The Plunge Moment
patterns.template: "[Person] / [water temp] / [round #]" with the body already entering the water at 0.0s
examples: 48°F. Round two. No backing out.
Her first plunge at Numa. Watch her face.

sources: Remedy Place plunge videos at 2.7M–2.8M TikTok views, and Business of Fashion says some #6minuteclub videos have "over 10 million views." Robb Report describes "shock on their faces" as the draw.  mechanism: skip rate covers the first 3 seconds (Instagram, August 2025
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: two posts in a row (fatigue), or with members who haven't consented to being filmed (sauna and plunge areas need explicit release). If it underperforms: move the cut earlier (start at water contact, not the step) or switch to `reaction-face`.
patterns.visual: Feet or legs breaking the water surface of a plunge, mid-motion. Temperature text in the top third.

patterns.name: First-Timer Reaction
patterns.template: "[Name]'s first [plunge/round/breathwork] — [timer]"
examples: Marcus said he'd last 10 seconds. Watch.
First plunge ever. Here we go.

sources: Remedy Place's "First timer" at 2.8M TikTok views. SweatHouz creator UGC is built on "I only lasted 30 seconds" reactions. A Bathhouse creator review reached about 35.5K likes
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: if the reaction looks like distress (it reads as unsafe), or with anyone who hasn't signed a media release. If it underperforms: pair two friends (`bring-a-friend-duo`) so the reaction becomes social, not solo.
patterns.visual: Tight face shot at the instant of cold contact, eyes wide, with the plunge visible.

patterns.name: On-Screen Clock
patterns.template: "[Timer 00:00] — can [name] make it to [time]?"
examples: Goal: 3 minutes. Clock's running.
First try: 0:45. Next visit: ?

sources: Remedy Place's #6minuteclub turns time-in-water into a shareable achievement; Business of Fashion quotes it as "a very shareable moment."  mechanism: watch time is a top-3 signal (Mosseri, January 2025
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: never frame longer cold exposure as healthier or as a goal everyone should push toward. Keep it playful and include "go at your pace." If it underperforms: shorten the clock (30 to 60 seconds) and put the result in the first frame (`end-result-first`).
patterns.visual: Large running timer graphic over a person in the plunge or sauna.

patterns.name: Löyly / Steam Burst
patterns.template: "This is what [ritual name] sounds like" over water hitting stones
examples: The sound of our Finnish sauna waking up.
Ladle. Stones. Löyly. Wait for the wave.

sources: Othership's towel-waving explainer got about 10× its normal likes (1,002 vs 49–122). : practitioner guides recommend opening on a sharp sound in the first half second
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: if the footage is dim or noisy. Phone sensors struggle in sauna light, and a dark frame 0 raises skips. If it underperforms: add a 4-word text overlay ("What is löyly?") and a narrator line, turning it into `myth-or-question`.
patterns.visual: Ladle mid-pour, steam already rising off the stones. Warm, dark, high contrast.

patterns.name: Sound Before Sight
patterns.template: Sharp natural sound at 0.0s (hiss, splash, door latch) plus "[Sound] = [moment]"
examples: That hiss = round one.
The splash you'll hear all evening.

sources: practitioner guides, e.g. PromptsLove's scan of 79 outlier Reels). Caution: the oft-cited muted-viewing figures trace to a May 2016 Digiday report on Facebook, not Instagram, where publishers self-reported about 85% soundless views (PopSugar: 50–80%), so the text overlay is mandatory
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: as the only hook. Muted viewers get nothing without text.
patterns.visual: A close-up of the sound source (stones, water surface, cedar door) with the caption in large type for mute viewers.

patterns.name: POV Walk-In
patterns.template: "POV: your first [time/night] at [place]"
examples: POV: your first visit to Numa, start to finish.
POV: Tuesday 6pm in Midtown Mobile.

sources: widespread creator format). : SweatHouz creator UGC leans on "first visit" walk-throughs
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: if the walk-in shows an empty, unlit room. Emptiness reads as "nobody goes here." If it underperforms: start the POV at the most dramatic point (the plunge) and loop back to the door.
patterns.visual: First-person shot already moving through the door or toward the sauna. Movement starts at frame 0, not after.

patterns.name: Hot | Cold Split Screen
patterns.template: "[Hot temp]° | [Cold temp]° — [short invite]"
examples: 185° | 48°. Pick your order.
From cedar heat to cold water in a few steps.

sources: practitioners list "split screen before/after" as a no-words visual hook). Uses  facts NUMA controls (its own temperatures), which keeps it FTC-safe
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: if temperatures vary day to day. Only post numbers you actually maintain. If it underperforms: add a human in each half, since faces outperform rooms in the observed examples.
patterns.visual: Vertical split: glowing sauna left, blue plunge right, two huge numbers.

patterns.name: The Question First-Timers Actually Ask
patterns.template: "[Common question]?" + instructor answering on camera or slides
examples: Sauna first or plunge first? Here's how we run it at Numa.
Do I need to know what I'm doing? No. A guide walks you through it.

sources: practitioners: put the promise first). : Metricool found posts with CTAs get 203% more comments, so end with "drop your question."
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: if the honest answer requires a health claim ("will this help my arthritis?"). Redirect those to a physician, not a Reel. If it underperforms: convert it into a carousel (`first-timer-faq`), where saves are measured higher.
patterns.visual: Instructor mid-sentence, looking at the lens, question in bold top-third text.

patterns.name: First-Timer Guide Carousel
patterns.template: Cover: "Your first [visit]: [n] things to know" · Slide 2: standalone rehook
examples: First time at Numa? 7 things nobody tells you.
What to bring, wear and expect, in one swipe.

sources: Carousels lead save rate (0.05% vs 0.04% Reels, Socialinsider). Buffer: 6.9% engagement by reach. The slide-2 re-serve is from Mosseri
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: as the only format in a week. Carousels deepen; they don't discover at your size. If it underperforms: add music (Mosseri: makes carousels eligible for Reels surfaces) and rework slide 2.
patterns.visual: Real photo of the sauna with people, a large number, a warm palette. Slide 2: a different strong image plus "Swimsuit or towel? Both work."

patterns.name: What It Actually Looks Like
patterns.template: "What you think [X] is / what it actually is at [place]"
examples: What you think a sauna studio is: silent, intimidating. What Numa is: this.
Breathwork: you expect weird. You get a calm Tuesday night with your neighbors.

sources: Bathhouse's own "Bathhouse vs spa, what's the difference?" overlay hook. Othership positions itself as social, not silent.  numbers on brand posts (85 likes) suggest it works better voiced by people than by the brand
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: if "reality" implies outcomes ("you'll leave pain-free"). If it underperforms: let a member deliver it (`member-experience-voice`).
patterns.visual: Split or quick-cut: stock-style "intimidating spa" vs real warm crowd.

patterns.name: The $49 Line
patterns.template: "$[price]. [Time]. [What's included]."
examples: $49. Discover Numa: your first month, one time, no commitment.
Discover Numa: three classes, three red light sessions, unlimited Flow Space.

sources: direct-response practice).  context: Metricool found CTA posts get 92% more saves. FTC: state offer terms clearly (new clients, one month

patterns.visual: Price in huge type over motion (plunge or steam), never over a static logo.

patterns.name: Mobile, This Is Yours
patterns.template: "[City/neighborhood], you have a [unique thing] now."
examples: Mobile, you have a Finnish sauna and cold plunges now. In Midtown.
Midtown Mobile's new weeknight plan.

sources: mechanism: sends weigh more for non-follower reach (Mosseri). "Mobile" in text and caption helps location relevance (Mosseri has said hashtags help Instagram understand topic, not raise reach
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: in back-to-back weeks, because it reads as a billboard. If it underperforms: make it about a specific local moment (`seasonal-weather`).
patterns.visual: Recognizable local cue (street sign, live oak, skyline) cutting straight into the sauna. Text names the city.

patterns.name: Weather-Jacked Hook
patterns.template: "It's [weather] in [city]. Here's [contrast]."

First cold front of the year. Perfect sauna night.

sources: timeliness

patterns.visual: Weather app screenshot or sweaty-street shot, hard cut to plunge or sauna.

patterns.name: Numa Nights Energy
patterns.template: "This was [event] last [day]. Next one: [date]."

One sauna, one playlist, a room full of neighbors.

patterns.template: Frame 1: "[Event] in [n] days" + countdown sticker

patterns.name: Built for the DM

Send this to whoever owes you a weeknight plan.

sources: mechanism. Sends per reach is the key signal for unconnected reach (Mosseri, January 2025). Reels hold the highest share rate (0.10%, Socialinsider). The pattern itself

patterns.name: Two Friends, One Plunge

Towel down, voices low, ladle etiquette: the Numa basics.

I came for the sauna, I stay for the people.

sources: Creator/guest voices outperform brand voices at Bathhouse and SweatHouz. FTC: testimonials are the advertiser's claims, so edit out any health outcome ("my back pain is gone"
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.visual: Member's face or hands with the quote large.

What happens before the first session of the day.

sources: behind-the-scenes is a common recommendation). Socialinsider notes Reels fit "authentic behind-the-scenes glimpses."
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.visual: Thermometer climbing or lights flicking on, with a time stamp in the corner.

examples: Your feed is loud. Our sauna isn't.
Pause here for 5 seconds.

sources: pattern-interrupt theory). There is a risk: most data favors motion at frame 0 (practitioners argue "motion in frame 1"

Listen for the splash.

patterns.name: Story Poll Opener
patterns.template: "[Binary question]?" + poll sticker on frame 1
examples: Hot person or cold person?
Sauna before or after work?

evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.visual: Split hot/cold image with the poll centered.

patterns.name: Myth vs Fact
patterns.template: Hook -> Myth 1 -> Myth 2 -> Myth 3 -> Payoff + send line -> Loop tail
examples: Three things people get wrong before their first Numa visit.
Send this to the friend who keeps saying 'one day.'

sources: Sends weighted for unconnected reach (**OS**, Mosseri January 2025). Numbered-list structure (**PC**). Myths must be about the *experience*, not physiology; "myth: cold plunges speed recovery" framed either way is a health claim needing RCT-level substantiation (**OS**, FTC 2022
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: Failure signs and fix: Skip rate above your median (or ~50%+) means the hook is abstract; open on the strongest myth said straight to camera, with text in frame 1. Retention cliff after myth 1 means the myths are too similar; reorder so the most surprising comes second. Saves fine but sends under ~5 per 1K means there's no "person" to send it to; name the recipient ("your gym-averse partner").
beats: Hook (0–2 s): Text: "First visit myths ". Host walks into frame at the plunge, mid-motion.
Myth 2 (9–16 s): Guest sitting by the plunge, chatting.
Payoff + send line (24–30 s): Text overlay of the send line over the entry door.
Loop tail (30–32 s): Final frame matches the opening walk-in so it loops.

patterns.name: Relatable POV "Send-to" sketch
patterns.template: Hook -> Escalation -> Turn -> Send line
examples: POV: you brought your 'I don't do wellness' friend to Numa Nights.
Send to the friend you're bringing next time.

sources: Sends per reach is a top signal (**OS**). Short loops drive rewatches, and replays count as views and watch time (**OS**, Instagram help definitions). Sketch performance in local wellness is unmeasured (**AN**). Cast staff or friends who have consented. If the "friend" is staff, don't present it as
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: Failure signs and fix: High views but sends under ~5 per 1K means the premise is funny but not targetable; make the friend archetype more specific. Skip rate high means the opening frame reads as an ad; open on a face and the reaction, not the logo or the building.
beats: Hook (0–2 s): Text: "POV: you dragged your 'I don't do wellness' friend to Numa Nights". Friend with arms crossed at the door.
Send line (13–16 s): Text: "Send to the friend you're bringing next time."

patterns.name: First-Timer Reaction
patterns.template: Hook -> Setup -> Moment 1 -> Moment 2 (peak) -> Verdict -> Send line + disclosure
examples: I've never done any of this. Okay.
Send to your plunge buddy.

sources: Authenticity is consistently ranked first in what consumers want from brands; Sprout's 2022 Index found 39% want real customer testimonials or demos (**LS** survey). The FTC requires disclosure of material connections (a comped session) and bars outcome claims in testimonials without substantiation
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: Failure signs and fix: Drop at 8–12 s (setup too long) means you should cut straight from the hook to the sauna and move the plan into on-screen text. Low completion means the peak comes too late; move the plunge countdown to ~12–15 s. Profile visits fine but no follows means the bio doesn't say what Numa is or where it is; fix the bio line and pin this Reel.
beats: Hook (0–3 s): Text: "First time at Numa (real guest, unscripted)". Close-up on a nervous face.
Setup (3–8 s): Quick walkthrough, three cuts.
Moment 1 (8–18 s): Steam, close-ups, real reaction.
Moment 2 (peak) (18–28 s): Hold for the reaction, with no cut at the climax.
Send line + disclosure (36–40 s): Text: "Send to your plunge buddy" plus "Sam received a complimentary session."

patterns.name: Explainer
patterns.template: Hook -> Arrival -> Block 1 -> Block 2 -> Block 3 -> Save line -> Safety line
examples: Here's exactly what your first visit at Numa looks like.
Save this so you know the flow before you come.

sources: Socialinsider's 45–60 s bracket leads on engagement rate and median views (**LS**, H1 2026). Buffer's reach data shows little difference below 90 s (**LS**). "Time-stamped walkthrough" is practitioner-recommended for saves (**PC**). Describe the process, not effects (**OS**, FTC
evidence.notes: Seeded from docs/research (corrected by docs/research/REVIEW.md: Numa's facts win).

patterns.when_not: Failure signs and fix: Saves under ~3 per 1K means it reads as a promo, not a reference; add specifics like times, what to bring and price. Steep slope at 20–30 s means you're narrating what viewers can already see; cut words and let the visuals carry (target ~2.3 wps). High skip rate means "here's what happens" is generic; lead with a surprising detail ("no phones for 60 minutes").
beats: Block 1 (12–24 s): Sauna interior, timer on the wall, clock at 0:20.
Block 2 (24–36 s): Plunge; text "optional."
Save line (46–52 s): Text overlay plus booking cue.
Safety line (52–55 s): "Unsure if heat/cold is right for you? Check with your healthcare provider."

patterns.name: Transformation
patterns.template: Hook ("after" first) -> Rewind -> Process montage -> Return to "after" -> Send line
examples: Same Tuesday. Different evening.
